from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows", [
            "Vectors act as directed arrows in 2D space.",
            "Scale vectors using scalar multiplication.",
            "Add vectors using the head-to-tail method."
        ])
        
        # Define vectors
        u = Vector([1.5, 0.5], color="#FF6347") # Tomato
        v = Vector([0.5, 1.5], color="#4682B4") # SteelBlue
        
        # Place initially
        self.place_in_area(u, "B2", "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_in_area(v, "D2", "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        u_head = Dot(u.get_end(), color="#FF6347")
        u_glow = Dot(u.get_end(), color="#FF6347", radius=0.2).set_opacity(0.5).add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(u.get_end()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF6347")
        self.play(Create(u), Create(v))
        self.play(FadeIn(u_glow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#4682B4")
        self.play(u.animate.scale(1.5), v.animate.scale(0.5))
        self.play(FadeOut(u_glow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700") # Gold
        # Head-to-tail placement
        v_moved = v.copy().shift(u.get_end())
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(v, v_moved))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["A linear combination scales and adds vectors.", 
                         "Span is every point a combination can reach.", 
                         "Two non-parallel vectors sweep the entire plane."]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations and Span", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup vectors for animation
        u = Vector([1, 0.5], color=BLUE)
        v = Vector([-0.5, 1], color=YELLOW)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        
        span_area = Polygon(
            axes.c2p(-3, -3), axes.c2p(3, -3), axes.c2p(3, 3), axes.c2p(-3, 3),
            fill_color="#808080", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0
        )
        
        group = VGroup(axes, u, v, span_area)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(axes), GrowArrow(u), GrowArrow(v))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        dot = Dot(color=RED)
        self.add(dot)
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(1, 1)))
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(-0.5, 0.5)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GRAY)
        self.play(FadeIn(span_area))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of a Basis", [
            "A Basis is a minimalist spanning set.",
            "Basis vectors must be linearly independent.",
            "Every point has unique basis coordinates."
        ])

        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF7F")
        v1 = Vector([1, 2], color="#00FF7F")
        v2 = Vector([2, -0.5], color="#00FF7F")
        basis_group = VGroup(v1, v2).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        self.play(Create(basis_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF7F")
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(grid, "B2", "E5")
        self.play(FadeIn(grid), run_time=1.5)
        self.bring_to_front(basis_group)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF7F")
        w = Vector([1.5, 1], color=YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(w))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Span represents total reachable reach.",
            "Dependence means redundant, overlapping directions.",
            "Basis vectors define an efficient coordinate system."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Visualization", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Summarize the core concepts using a small map.
        dot_span = Dot(color=BLUE)
        circle_span = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE).set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        span_vgroup = VGroup(dot_span, circle_span)
        self.place_in_area(span_vgroup, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(span_vgroup))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate a smooth zoom-out showing the interplay of span, dependence, and basis.
        line1 = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=RED)
        line2 = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.2 + UP*0.5, color=RED)
        dependence_group = VGroup(line1, line2).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(dependence_group, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Transform(span_vgroup, dependence_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final appearance of the summary text, highlighted with #FFD700 (Gold) flashing.
        basis_group = VGroup(
            Vector(RIGHT, color=GOLD),
            Vector(UP, color=GOLD)
        )
        self.place_in_area(basis_group, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Transform(span_vgroup, basis_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        self.play(Flash(self.lecture[2], color=GOLD, line_length=0.2, num_lines=12))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Span to Basis

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as directed quantities in 2D space. Explain that we can scale them (scalar multiplication) and connect them head-to-tail (vector addition).
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Robot Arm' in 2D: Two segments that can stretch and rotate to reach any point.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Define a linear combination as adding scaled vectors (c1v1 + c2v2). Define 'Span' as the collection of all possible points reachable through these combinations. Use a grid animation to show how two non-parallel vectors sweep across the 2D plane.
sections.example: If a squirrel can jump in vector v1 and vector v2, the 'Span' is the entire territory the squirrel can reach in the park.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector
sections.content: Explain linear dependence as the existence of 'redundancy'. If one vector lies on the line of another, it adds no new reach. Visually show a vector shrinking to zero or overlapping, indicating it can be 'represented' by others.
sections.example: Three delivery drones where one drone's path is just the sum of the other two; the third drone is 'linearly dependent' and unnecessary for the mission.

sections.title: The Concept of a Basis
sections.content: Define a Basis as the 'minimalist' set: vectors that span the space without any redundancy (linearly independent). Explain that every vector in the space can be represented by a unique set of coordinates using the basis.
sections.example: A GPS coordinate system: The unit vectors 'East' and 'North' serve as the basis. Every location on the map is just a unique linear combination of these two.

sections.title: Summary & Visualization
sections.content: Recap: Span (reach), Linear Dependence (overlap), and Basis (efficient coordinate system). Show a 3D animation where removing a dependent vector collapses a volume into a plane, demonstrating why bases are essential for defining dimensions.
sections.example: An architect designing a room: The basis vectors are the corners of the floor; if the vectors aren't independent, the room collapses into a flat line!
